title: Legal evidence + owner adoption register
decision: Owner decision, 6 October 2026 (GS-LEGAL-001): no solicitor is commissioned at this stage; GS-O003's mandatory solicitor approval is replaced by an evidence-based review of each document against current UK legislation and official guidance, followed by explicit owner adoption. Nothing in this register claims solicitor review, certification or guaranteed enforceability.
rules: Only the owner moves a document to OWNER_ADOPTED, by recording ownerAdoptedOn (date) and ownerAdoptedVersion (the exact version adopted). No script sets either.
PUBLISHABLE requires OWNER_ADOPTED plus a passing check:legal:adoption run on the adopted version; ownerAdoptedVersion must equal the document's version.
scripts/migrate-production-cms.mjs admits a legal document to the production payload only at PUBLISHABLE.

An adopted entry records adoptionAuthority (the owner's instruction) and its publicationPrerequisites; PUBLISHABLE is refused while any prerequisite has no recorded evidence in prerequisitesMet. Adoption is never inferred: a document carrying an open marker cannot be OWNER_ADOPTED.

GS-LEGAL-001-R4 review: an adoption is bound to the adopted text by ownerAdoptedSha256 (the draft file's sha256, or for client-terms the sha256 of its generated content); check:legal:adoption refuses an adopted entry whose text no longer matches, so an edit that keeps the version number cannot keep the adoption. Privacy, when adopted, must list H4-B-INTAKE-PROMOTED and does not list itself.

GS-LEGAL-001-R6: an adopted document that describes an operation as already happening needs recorded evidence of it at adoption (REQUIRED_ADOPTION_EVIDENCE). Privacy needs RETENTION-ROUTINE-OPERATING, because its section 8 describes the scheduled retention reviews.

GS-LEGAL-001-R6 review: privacy adoption also needs HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN evidence, so removing the section 6 marker alone cannot unblock adoption. (Redefined at R7 and again at R8; see the R8 rule. The R6 definition is superseded.)
GS-LEGAL-001-R7: HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN was redefined and kept. (Superseded at R8; see the next rule.)

GS-LEGAL-001-R8: HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN verifies the real processing arrangement: (1) Gridsmith manages its website hosting; (2) Gridsmith's admin department manages the hosting account and its administrative access; (3) Hostinger supplies the hosting infrastructure; (4) website hosting in France; (5) email hosting through Hostinger; (6) the privacy policy describes them accurately; (7) Gridsmith Ltd is the Customer bound by Hostinger's terms for the gridsmith.uk website and mailbox (UK GDPR Art. 28(3)), so that the policy's reliance on Hostinger's transfer safeguards is accurate and Hostinger's notices reach a Gridsmith-controlled address. The minimum is that the website and mailbox sit under a Hostinger account whose Customer is Gridsmith Ltd; changing the existing account as a whole is not required. An owner risk decision instead records an accepted Art. 28(3) non-compliance, not satisfaction of element 7. No inter-company agreement or account history is required (not required; R9 route B is one optional route) (research/GS-LEGAL-001/R8-HOSTING-RETENTION-CLOSURE.md section 2.3). (Element 7 restated at R9; the R8 minimum, a Gridsmith Ltd Customer account, is withdrawn. See the R9 rule.)

GS-LEGAL-001-R9: element 7 of HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN is an Art. 28(3) arrangement binding Hostinger's processing of gridsmith.uk data with regard to Gridsmith Ltd, with Hostinger's notices reaching Gridsmith. UK GDPR does not require Gridsmith Ltd to be the named Hostinger customer, and no new account, subscription, domain, VPS or migration is required. Hostinger's Terms (section 4) make the Account-information entity the owner of the Account's data and Services, so the current terms alone do not evidence it. Close it by (A) the Account information listing Gridsmith Ltd, or (B) a documented processor chain with the Account owner under DPA section 2.2, which needs a Privacy section 6/7 edit (research/GS-LEGAL-001/R9-RETENTION-HOSTINGER-REASSESSMENT.md section 3.4). Evidence keys go in prerequisitesMet on the privacy entry; adoption itself remains the owner's act.

GS-LEGAL-001-R10: HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN moved from privacy adoption evidence to a privacy publication prerequisite. Privacy 2.3 section 7 describes Hostinger's transfer safeguards without claiming Gridsmith relies on them, so the adopted text does not depend on the chain; PUBLISHABLE is still refused until it is evidenced. The hosting infrastructure decision is closed by the owner (existing Hostinger account; no migration or ownership change). The chain stays open until the arrangement in operations/HOSTING-PROCESSING-ARRANGEMENT-DRAFT.md, or an equivalent, is executed. The gap affects current processing on the account (the mailbox) until signature; the owner's acceptance of that risk is not compliance. When privacy is adopted, the HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN prerequisite's requirement must read: arrangement executed, a UK transfer mechanism if the account owner is outside the UK, and Privacy sections 6 and 7 reviewed against it (research/GS-LEGAL-001/R10-HOSTING-CLOSEOUT-PRIVACY-PACKAGE.md).

GS-LEGAL-001-R11: the owner explicitly adopts Privacy 2.3 effective 8 October 2026, bound to SHA-256 80e67b5256449e2c7fc1562ead2da8ec538b217c8735cba3679f985af50a620b. R8-R10 interpretations requiring a separate account-holder agreement are superseded by the clarified internal administration facts and focused current Terms/DPA reading. HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN now records existing Article 28 coverage (authorised corporate service use under Terms sections 1-3 plus incorporated DPA), not execution of the superseded draft. It is evidenced on that basis; no new provider agreement or account change was executed. Internal staff are not separate processors; shared personnel do not merge legal entities. Reassess only if a separate entity actually processes Gridsmith data. CUTOVER-AUTHORITY and H4-B-INTAKE-PROMOTED remain unmet; Privacy and all six earlier adopted documents stay OWNER_ADOPTED, not PUBLISHABLE. See research/GS-LEGAL-001/R11-PRIVACY-ADOPTION-HOSTING-CLOSEOUT.md.

Not ready for adoption. 8 October 2026 (GS-LEGAL-001-R10): the privacy policy draft moved to version 2.3 (one section 7 sentence; draft sha256 d388e844...), OWNER_REVIEW_REQUIRED with no adoption fields, and is ready for the owner's explicit adoption. RETENTION-ROUTINE-OPERATING is recorded. HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN is now a publication prerequisite and remains unmet; an unexecuted draft processing arrangement is prepared (research/GS-LEGAL-001/R10-HOSTING-CLOSEOUT-PRIVACY-PACKAGE.md). 8 October 2026 (GS-LEGAL-001-R11): Privacy 2.3 OWNER_ADOPTED on explicit owner approval; header-only change; exact adopted SHA-256 80e67b5256449e2c7fc1562ead2da8ec538b217c8735cba3679f985af50a620b. All seven OWNER_ADOPTED; earlier six entries and fingerprints unchanged. Existing infrastructure decision CLOSED. HOSTINGER-PROCESSOR-CHAIN evidenced from owner-attested authorised corporate use and current Terms/DPA; no separate administrator agreement shown necessary. R10 draft SUPERSEDED / NOT EXECUTED. No legal document PUBLISHABLE, published or deployed.
